conventions.convention: Density operators are non-negative, hence self-adjoint, trace-one endomorphisms on nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces. Support is the orthogonal complement of the kernel; faithfulness on S requires support exactly S and positive-definite restriction to S.

The root inner product is linear in its first argument. The outer product |x⟩⟨y| sends z to ⟨z,y⟩x. Pure states are rays under nonzero complex scalar multiplication; unit representatives of one ray differ by a scalar of modulus one.

An effect E has both E and I−E non-negative. A finite complete positive family is a nonempty finite list of non-negative endomorphisms summing to identity; this definition supplies no measurement law.

Finite ensembles have at least one component, nonnegative real weights summing to one, and density-operator components even at zero weights. Purifications are unit vectors in H⊗K, with H first and auxiliary K contracted by partial trace.

Schmidt coefficients in the displayed decomposition are strictly positive. The zero vector uses r=0 and an empty sum; zero-dimensional tensor factors are allowed. For coefficient matrix C, the second Schmidt family's coordinates are conjugates of the right singular vectors.

Purification equivalence holds for every common padding dimension m at least both auxiliary dimensions and every pair of linear isometric embeddings into standard C^m. The unitary acts on the padded auxiliary factor and maps purification 2 to purification 1.
The ensemble correspondence uses square roots of the grouped effects themselves. Zero-weight outcomes have effect zero; the unused auxiliary complement is assigned to an outcome of positive weight.

load_bearing.statement: A density operator on nonzero finite-dimensional complex H is a non-negative endomorphism ρ:H→H with tr(ρ)=1.
For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces H,K and every Ψ∈H⊗K, there are r≥0, positive s₁,…,sᵣ, and orthonormal families uⱼ∈H,vⱼ∈K such that Ψ=Σⱼsⱼuⱼ⊗vⱼ and ‖Ψ‖²=Σⱼsⱼ². For Ψ=0 take r=0.

For nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product H, the map sending a ray [u] to the rank-one projector P_u=|u⟩⟨u| of any unit representative is well-defined and bijective onto the rank-one orthogonal projections on H. Each P_u is non-negative and has trace one.
Every density operator ρ on nonzero finite-dimensional complex H has ρ=Σⱼ₌₁ᵐλⱼ|eⱼ⟩⟨eⱼ|, where m=rank(ρ)≥1, the λⱼ are positive and sum to one, and the eⱼ are orthonormal unit vectors.

A finite ensemble's barycenter is a density operator. Regrouping outcomes into blocks, using normalized block barycenters for positive block weights, preserves the overall barycenter; zero-total-weight blocks contribute zero.

Every density operator has a purification with auxiliary dimension rank(ρ). For any two finite-dimensional purifications, every common padding dimension m≥max(dim K₁,dim K₂), and every pair of linear isometric embeddings ιᵢ:Kᵢ→C^m, there is a unitary U on C^m with (I⊗U)(I⊗ι₂)Ψ₂=(I⊗ι₁)Ψ₁.
Every nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space H admits a density operator; specifically, if d=dim_C H, then I_H/d is a density operator on H.
For nonzero finite-dimensional complex H, every member E_a of a finite complete positive family is an effect: E_a and I_H−E_a are non-negative.

alerts.finding: In F1, lem-qc-faithful-state-dominates-positive-operator says: “This current draft definition is present, but its declared existence supplier remains unresolved.” The current declared supplier thm-qc-density-operator-existence explicitly constructs I_H/d and proves positivity and trace one. The unresolved-supplier description is stale; this finding concerns the contextual sentence, not the domination argument.

In F2, thm-qc-trace-distance-range-and-equality says: “The current QC03 definition is present as a draft; its declared existence supplier is still unresolved.” The current thm-qc-density-operator-existence supplies the construction I_H/d with a local proof. The unresolved-supplier description is stale.

F5 attributes to thm-qc-ray-projector-well-defined-and-bijective that the projector is “a positive trace-one density operator.” The supplier says “non-negative,” and def-non-negative-and-positive-operator reserves “positive” for positive definite. A rank-one projector in dimension greater than one has a nontrivial kernel. The probability argument uses only non-negativity, so this is a terminology/citation wording issue.

F8 attributes to thm-qc-ray-projector-well-defined-and-bijective that the projector is “a positive trace-one density operator.” The supplier establishes non-negativity, whereas the root definition of “positive” requires positive definiteness. A unit-ray projector in dimension greater than one is not positive definite. The branch argument needs only the supplier's non-negative trace-one conclusion.

Product bases, tensor maps and auxiliary-index contraction match the suppliers. Schmidt families are completed before using basis-independent partial trace.
Phase kickback uses a normalized target as a pure-state representative, consistent with the ray definition.
The outcome kernel uses unit-ray projectors as density operators; the superposition law uses non-negative trace-one inputs without treating a zero-probability branch as a normalized state.
Coset mixtures and transformed rank-one states use the non-negative trace-one definition on nonzero finite registers.
The good/bad decomposition uses normalized vector representatives under 0<t<N.
Prepared states are unit representatives on nonzero H; zero components are omitted at success weights zero and one.

The coherent sampler supplies a unitary output with distinct sample labels and unit work vectors; zero-probability labels cause no normalization problem.
The page-level prerequisite introduces no stronger state assertion; no direct assigned-item citation was found among its listed items.
Witnesses are density operators on nonzero registers, including the one-dimensional zero-qubit register. The pure-witness argument uses non-negative spectral weights summing to one.
Message densities and swap-test inputs use non-negative trace-one operators and unit-ray projectors; repeated fingerprints retain normalized tensor-product states.
Isometric evolution preserves density operators; the history-state output uses a finite mixture of unit-vector projectors.
POVMs enumerate finite complete positive families faithfully. Outcome and conditional-state arguments retain non-negativity, trace one and positive-probability conditioning.
Channel properties are stated on full operator spaces, including permitted zero-dimensional cases; this does not assert existence of density operators on zero spaces.
Density, faithfulness, ray-projector and Schmidt propositions are used faithfully. Two stale comments about unresolved density existence are separately reported as alerts.
Bloch positivity uses non-negative trace-one matrices; sphere purity uses rank-one orthogonal projectors and the ray bijection.
Global-phase, relative-phase and reflection arguments use the same ray equivalence. The entanglement verification correctly relates coefficient-matrix rank to every Schmidt decomposition.
The ray and density uses are substantively compatible, including zero-qubit registers, but two facts restate non-negative projectors as “positive”; exact wording issues are reported in alerts.
The page's state and branch descriptions introduce no stronger claim about density operators or rays; no direct assigned-item citation was found among its listed items.
Projective charts, chord distance and preparation targets use nonzero-scalar ray equivalence, reducing to unit phases for unit representatives.
